subject: Design: rolling trust anchors and KEK handoff for on-prem bundles
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Payments Infra <infra-team@acme-payments.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Design: rolling trust anchors and KEK handoff for on-prem bundles

Team —

I sketched a lightweight proposal for how we can manage rolling Key Encryption Keys (KEKs) and trust anchors for Redwood Private installs that will be shipped into customer VPCs/on-prem. The goal: provide frequent cryptographic refreshes (monthly/quarterly) without operator downtime and with clear audit traces for BYOK customers.

High-level approach (attached PDF):
- A trust-anchor set per customer (root public keys) stored in the local config bundle; signed snapshots distributed via manifest service.
- KEKs are short-lived wrapping keys generated in the customer HSM (or by our KMS when BYOK isn't possible), with server-side ephemeral wrapping keys for per-instance envelopes.
- Rolling plan: staggered anchor snapshot + KEK rewrap every N days; wire a two-phase commit across replicas to avoid cache invalidation windows.
- Operator-eviction safepoint: include a signed zeroize checkpoint that the operator must co-sign to proceed with manual intervention; otherwise automatic fallback to previous valid anchor.

Open questions I want your input on:
1) Acceptable rotation cadence for enterprise customers (monthly vs 90 days).
2) How tightly do we couple KEK lifetime to session/tenant tokens — do we require rewrap on role refresh?
3) Audit evidence we need in the bundle for customers to satisfy their auditors (attestation artifacts, timestamps, and operator signatures).

I've attached the initial PDF and a sample attestation text file for our HSM vendor. Please review before EOD Wednesday; I'd like to propose a PoC plan to Acme next week.

Attachments: [kek-rolling-trust-anchors-v1.pdf (PDF); poa-attestation-sample.txt (TXT)]

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Product Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Acme Payments Infra <infra-team@acme-payments.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Design: rolling trust anchors and KEK handoff for on-prem bundles

+1 on the proposal, good call on manifest-signed snapshots. A few practical concerns from an ops/upgrade perspective:

- Staggering: we should allow configurable windows per customer. Some infra teams (banking) will *only* accept monthly maintenance windows. Make the default conservative and allow opt-in to faster cadence.
- Two-phase commit across replicas: important. Can we leverage existing config rollout/leader lease rather than inventing a separate coordinator? That reduces network ports we need to open.
- Operator zeroize co-sign: we need a strictly defined operator identity (service-account vs human) and an auditable token exchange. We should avoid human-in-the-loop blockers for emergency key revocation.

On evidence for auditors: the sample attestation is helpful. Suggest we include these elements in the bundle by default:
  * signed manifest (manifest sig from our control plane + customer key signature when BYOK)
  * per-KEK audit record (HSM log reference + time + nonce)
  * rewrap proof (old->new key thumbprints)

I'll annotate the PDF with inline comments and push a short ops checklist. If this lines up, I'm happy to lead the PoC runbook.

On cadence: propose default 90 days, with monthly as an enterprise opt-in.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Hi Diego / Marissa —

Thanks for looping Aurelia in. A few notes from the vendor/integration angle:

1) Attestation artifacts: our customers typically require an HSM attestation bundle that includes:
   - Hardware attestation statement (certificate chain)
   - A signed PCR-like statement with boot measurements (if available)
   - Signed nonce response for on-demand attestations

   The "poa-attestation-sample.txt" looks fine, but the JSON Web Attestation (JWA) format is more common for modern auditors. Can you provide a mapping?

2) KEK rewrap without egress: if the KEK material must always remain inside the customer boundary, our preferred approach is local rewrap via an HSM-initiated operation. That means Redwood bundles a rewrap request (opaque) but the HSM performs the wrap/unwrap locally and only emits a thumbprint. Does your manifest protocol allow opaque requests like that?

3) Emergency revocation: for customers that enforce zero-operator capability, we need to support an out-of-band revocation channel (signed by the customer's governance key) that the instance will accept without operator interaction. This needs careful TTLing to avoid accidental lockouts.

We can demo an HSM side rewrap flow with Acme next Thursday. We'll bring an example attestation in JWA and sample challenge-response logs.

Regards,
Aurelia Ops
Aurelia Secure (integration partner)
ops@aureliasec.com

Thanks — great feedback. Summary and next actions: 

1) Cadence: default 90d, enterprise opt-in monthly. Marissa to produce PoC runbook (ops checklist + leader-lease approach) by Fri EOD.
2) HSM attestation: Aurelia to provide a JWA mapping and sample signed nonce flow. Dieg0? (typo) — please make sure our manifest schema can carry an opaque rewrap request and receive a thumbprint-only response.
3) Emergency revocation: add an optional governance-key channel to manifest parser with clear TTL and a documented fallthrough to a signed previous-anchor snapshot.
4) PoC timeline: demo with Acme on Thu (2028-06-13) at 10:00 PT. Acme asked for an HSM-side rewrap example and an attestation artifact; Aurelia will bring examples.

Immediate asks for this thread:
- Marissa: confirm you'll lead the PoC runbook and share the first draft by Fri (2028-06-09).
- Tessa: work with infra to determine if the leader-lease approach can piggyback on our existing config republish port (443/7443) — short note with constraints by Wed EOD.
- Vivek: please flag any control-plane policy implications for manifest signing that could impact hosted customers.

I'll update the design doc (linked) with the revised manifest schema and the emergency-revocation state machine. If anyone wants an internal review session, I can schedule 30m tomorrow.

Thanks,
